To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cannabinoid inhibition of adenlylate cyclase in N18TG2 neuroblastoma cells is a function of both potency and efficacy.
the cannabinoids inhibit the enzyme adenylate cyclases in neuroblastoma cells, and that the metabolites of the drugs are often more potent than the original drugs.
delta 9THCA, a major constituent of marihuana, inhibits the activity of adenlyate cyclase in neuroblastoma cells and that this effect is mimicked by a series of metabolites of delta9THC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of cannabinoids and the development of selective antagonists.
the development of a quantitative pharmacological model for cannabinoids which may be useful in the evaluation of new compounds and the elucidation of their mechanism of action.
the development and application of new analytical methods to determine the chemical constituents of cannabis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of adenylcyclase is not the sole or primary site of cannabinoid action.
cannabinoids with an unsaturated alkyl side chain are active inhibitors of adenylate cylase.
delta 9THCs inhibition of adenylates cyclase is a pharmacologically relevant phenomenon and may be a mechanism of cannabinoid action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cannabinoids are more effective in producing pharmacologic effects when they are hydroxylated in positions that do not affect their ability to bind to cannabinoid receptors.

the cannabinoids are a family of drugs which have a common mechanism of action and which differ in the degree to which this mechanism contributes to the overall pharmacological effect of each compound.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the cannabinoids are not a homogeneous group of compounds, and that the effects of the cannabinoids on the adenylate cyclasc activity in neuroblastoma cells are not necessarily predictive of effects on other biological systems.
THC and its metabolites are not only the most active compounds in the cannabis plant, but that they also are the most potent at inhibiting the adenylate cyclases of the human body.
the pharmacology of the cannabinoid receptor system in the brain is not the same as the pharmacology of this receptor system in peripheral organs, such as the immune system.
